question: On 1 September 2026, the Greek Government announced the completion of the physical implementation of 123 milestones and targets that will be included in the final payment request, amounting to EUR 6.7 billion1. However, in May, Greece requested a further revision of the recovery and resilience plan (RRP), stating that part of it was no longer achievable.

The final revision was adopted shortly before the 31 August deadline and affected 111 measures: one was removed, while others were modified due to delays in public procurement, lower demand or technical challenges2. For example, the energy renovation target for residential buildings was reduced from 105 000 to 69 730 (-33.

6 %), while in primary healthcare, the renovation of 156 units became 146 and the training of 10 000 professionals turned into 6 172 who had merely started a training programme3. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What differences in physical and financial scope – overall and broken down by measure – are there between Greece’s initial and final RRP?
Given the aforementioned reductions in scope, is it possible to present the initially approved RRP as complete?
It the Commission’s view, which of the 123 milestones were unfulfilled by 31 August 2026, and which corresponding funding reduction will be applied under Article 24 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2414?
